summary.oneLiner: R.P.P Infra is a mid-sized EPC player with a robust ₹3,750cr order book, but faces severe margin compression due to shift from self-executed to subcontracted projects and rising input costs. Recovery is expected from Q2FY27 as new self-executed projects ramp up, though near-term profitability remains under pressure.

one-line thesis: R.P.P Infra is a mid-sized EPC player with a robust ₹3,750cr order book, but faces severe margin compression due to shift from self-executed to subcontracted projects and rising input costs. Recovery is expected from Q2FY27 as new self-executed projects ramp up, though near-term profitability remains under pressure.
guidance / outlook: Management expects improved profitability from Q2FY27 as newly awarded self-executed projects (including BHEL-related) begin revenue contribution; focus on increasing own-execution volume and cost control.
order book & pipeline: ₹3750.83cr outstanding (as of Mar 2026), including ₹2470.14cr newly awarded in FY26 (9 infrastructure, 1 building, 1 water project)
segment / subsidiary detail: Infrastructure: ₹2096.26cr (9 projects); Buildings: ₹8.03cr (1 project); Water management: ₹365.85cr (1 project); Total new awards FY26: ₹2470.14cr
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Sri Lanka (piling approved, building permit pending); potential to capture more public infrastructure tenders in India; scaling self-execution model to improve margins
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin fell to 7.33% (from 14.20% in FY25); EBITDA margin at 2.36% (from 7.48%); driven by higher subcontracting, material/fuel/labor inflation, and non-recurring project losses
capex / expansion: Not disclosed; implied capex is minimal as business is EPC-driven with asset-light model
capital allocation: Prioritizing working capital for new project execution; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on debt reduction and margin recovery
risks & watch-items: High dependence on subcontracting eroding margins; delays in project commencement; cost inflation (materials, labor); regulatory delays in Sri Lanka project; concentration risk in few large clients
non-obvious takeaways: Despite declining profits, order book grew 66% YoY — indicating strong pipeline; the drop in PAT is structural (mix shift), not operational failure; auditor’s report is clean despite financial stress

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
